brief.headline: Add a proof step so Opus verifies its own PR before you wake up
brief.summary:
Two plugins give you a real verification gate tonight. fablize forces Opus through a completion-evidence-verification procedure, and fable-method ships the same think/act/prove loop as Claude Code skills for any model — install one and run it on a real task before you trust an unattended session. Claude Code 2.1.246 now warns on wildcard Bash allow rules, so check your /permissions Auto mode list tonight; a rule like Bash(git * main) can match more than you meant. If you delegate to separate agents, amElnagdy/delegate-skills lands each implementer's diff for your review, and cobusgreyling/loop-engineering gives you loop-audit and loop-cost to sanity-check a loop before it runs all night.

On cost, opencodex lets Claude Code and Codex call Ollama or other providers directly, and Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a gateway, so route routine subagent calls to a free local model instead of paying per call. Skip the $10k Mac Studio for local inference — a 24-32GB card plus OpenRouter credits buys more tokens per dollar, per a Reddit teardown — and if you want to push further, kimi-k3-in-c claims a 2.78T-parameter model running in 8GB of RAM on CPU alone, worth a benchmark before you trust it with anything unattended. Away from the desk, devspace turns the ChatGPT or Claude web app into a coding-agent trigger from a browser, and omnigent adds mobile check-in over your existing Claude Code/Codex/Cursor sessions. One real failure report worth reading: researchers showed LLMs can exploit bugs in self-hosted inference engines to take over the host machine, so audit sandboxing on any inference server your agents can reach.
bullets: Install fivetaku/fablize or Sahir619/fable-method to force an evidence-and-verification step before an agent calls a task done
Update to Claude Code 2.1.246 and review your Bash allow-rule wildcards under /permissions Auto mode
Wire in amElnagdy/delegate-skills to hand a task to a separate agent CLI per implementer and review the diff instead of babysitting
Run loop-audit and loop-cost from cobusgreyling/loop-engineering before trusting a loop to run overnight
Route routine subagent calls to a free local model via lidge-jun/opencodex or Ollama-as-gateway in Claude Desktop

Skip the $10k Mac Studio for local inference — a 24-32GB GPU plus OpenRouter credits wins on tokens per dollar, and audit sandboxing on any self-hosted inference engine since LLMs can exploit it to take over the host

signals.label: Self-verification loops
signals.note: fablize and fable-method both push a completion/evidence/proof step into the harness itself, independent of which model runs the task.

signals.label: Cheap and local model routing
signals.note: opencodex, Ollama-as-gateway in Claude Desktop, Fuxi's cost-aware routing, and a CPU-only 2.78T model all point at moving work off metered API calls.

signals.label: Agent infrastructure as attack surface
signals.note: A demonstrated exploit against self-hosted inference engines plus a new agent-driven CVE scanner show more attention on the agent's own runtime, not just its output.

signals.label: Away-from-desk control
signals.note: devspace, omnigent's mobile check-in, and nodeterm's browser Server Edition are all adding ways to steer or watch agents without being at your terminal.

items.title: lidge-jun/opencodex — Universal provider proxy for OpenAI Codex & Claude Code — use any LLM (Claude, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek, Ollama…) with Codex CLI, App, SDK, and Claude Code
items.tldr: opencodex adds a universal provider proxy so Codex CLI/App/SDK and Claude Code can run against Claude, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek, or local Ollama models.
items.whyItMatters: Lets you keep your Claude Code/Codex workflow while routing individual calls to cheaper or local models.
items.tryThis: Clone lidge-jun/opencodex and point Claude Code's model endpoint at an Ollama-served local model for routine subagent work.

items.title: cobusgreyling/loop-engineering — Practical patterns, starters & CLI tools for loop engineering with AI coding agents. Design systems that prompt and orchestrate agents (inspired by Addy Osmani and Boris Cherny). Includes loop-audit, loop-in
items.tldr: loop-engineering is a CLI toolkit (loop-audit, loop-init, loop-cost) for building and checking agent loops before letting them run unattended.
items.whyItMatters: loop-audit and loop-cost give concrete ways to check an agent loop's behavior and spend before trusting it overnight.
items.tryThis: Run `loop-init` to scaffold an agent loop, then `loop-audit` before letting it run unattended overnight.

items.title: amElnagdy/delegate-skills — Delegate a coding task to a separate coding agent CLI, review the diff, land the commit yourself — one per implementer.
items.tldr: delegate-skills is a repo/skill that hands a task to a separate coding agent CLI, then lets you review its diff and land the commit yourself.
items.whyItMatters: Matches the "describe work, wake up to a reviewable PR" workflow directly, with one delegate agent per implementer instead of babysitting a single session.
items.tryThis: Clone amElnagdy/delegate-skills and wire it in as a skill for your next side task.

items.tldr: Claude Code 2.1.246 warns on wildcard Bash allow rules and adds an Auto mode tab in /permissions.
items.whyItMatters: A wildcard rule like Bash(git * main) can match flags you did not intend to allow. Check your existing Bash allow rules tonight.
items.tryThis: Update Claude Code, then review your Bash allow-rule wildcards under /permissions Auto mode.

items.title: FareedKhan-dev/kimi-k3-in-c — A 2.78-trillion-parameter Kimi K3 running inference on a single CPU in 8.24 GB of RAM. Portable C99: no BLAS, no framework, no GPU.
items.tldr: kimi-k3-in-c runs the 2.78-trillion-parameter Kimi K3 for inference on a single CPU in 8.24GB of RAM, in portable C99 with no GPU or BLAS.
items.whyItMatters: If it holds up, it puts a frontier-scale open model within reach of a machine you already own, for zero-cost background or offline agent tasks.
items.tryThis: Clone FareedKhan-dev/kimi-k3-in-c and benchmark it on a spare box before trusting it with anything unattended — verify quality and speed first.

items.title: oomol-lab/open-connector — Open-source auth gateway connecting 1000+ SaaS providers to AI agents through SDK, CLI, MCP, HTTP, and OpenAPI.
items.tldr: open-connector is an open-source auth gateway that connects 1000+ SaaS providers to agents over SDK, CLI, MCP, HTTP, and OpenAPI.
items.whyItMatters: Removes a chunk of the per-integration auth glue you'd otherwise write so an unattended agent can reach real services without you babysitting OAuth flows.
items.tryThis: Point a Claude Code MCP config at oomol-lab/open-connector to give a subagent authenticated access to a SaaS tool it needs mid-run.

items.title: CopilotKit/OpenBot — Open-source AI coworkers that each get a computer of their own: a browser, files and tools, with every action decided before it happens and recorded after. Bring any AG-UI agent.
items.tldr: CopilotKit released OpenBot, open-source agents that each get their own browser and files, with every action logged before and after it runs.
items.whyItMatters: This gives you a built-in audit trail for unattended agent runs, so you can check what an agent did before you review its PR.
items.tryThis: Clone CopilotKit/OpenBot and run one agent in a sandboxed browser session, then review its action log.

items.title: Sahir619/fable-method — The Fable Workflow: how Claude Fable 5 worked, distilled into skills any model can run, with the eval that keeps it honest. Think / act / prove.
items.tldr: fable-method distills the think/act/prove workflow behind Claude Fable 5 into Claude Code skills and an eval, usable with any model.
items.whyItMatters: Gives you a drop-in verification loop (evidence plus proof step) to make agent runs self-checking before you review the PR.
items.tryThis: Install the fable-method skills into Claude Code and run its eval against a real task to see the enforced proof step.

items.title: fuxicodex/Fuxi — FuXi is a fast, self-contained AI coding agent that lives in your terminal — edit code, run commands, and drive tools, with cost-aware routing across LLM providers.
items.tldr: Fuxi is a self-contained terminal coding agent with built-in cost-aware routing across LLM providers.
items.whyItMatters: Routes cheap subtasks to cheaper providers automatically instead of you hand-wiring a router in front of Claude Code.
items.tryThis: Run fuxicodex/Fuxi on a low-stakes task and check its routing decisions against what you'd pay running the same task through Claude Code alone.

items.title: eneskirca/nodeterm — Node-based terminal manager for AI coding agents — tmux-backed terminals and parallel agent sessions as draggable nodes on an infinite pan/zoom canvas. macOS, Linux, and a browser Server Edition.
items.tldr: nodeterm is a tmux-backed terminal manager that lays out parallel AI coding agent sessions as draggable nodes on an infinite canvas, with a browser Server Edition.
items.whyItMatters: Gives a way to supervise many unattended agent sessions at once, including checking on them from a browser away from your desk.
items.tryThis: Clone eneskirca/nodeterm and try the Server Edition to check agent sessions from a browser tonight.

items.title: larlarua/AutoCVE — Agent-driven automated CVE discovery platform for source code auditing, vulnerability verification, and report generation.
items.tldr: larlarua released AutoCVE, an agent-driven platform that finds, verifies, and reports CVEs from source code.
items.whyItMatters: You can bolt this onto your pipeline as a security-verification step before you merge an overnight PR.
items.tryThis: Clone larlarua/AutoCVE and run it against a repo to get a vulnerability report.

items.title: fivetaku/fablize — A Claude Code plugin that makes Opus behave like Fable — completion, evidence, and verification enforced as procedure. Ships only what a Fable-vs-Opus comparison proved transferable.
items.tldr: fablize is a Claude Code plugin that forces Opus to follow the completion/evidence/verification procedure a Fable-vs-Opus comparison found transferable.
items.whyItMatters: Adds an enforced verification step to Opus runs so you get a checked PR instead of an agent that just claims it's done.
items.tryThis: Install fivetaku/fablize as a Claude Code plugin and run it on your next Opus-driven task to see the evidence/verification gate in action.

items.title: Show HN: Screen memory without screenshots, just text to Markdown
items.tldr: A new macOS app reads your active window text every few seconds and writes it to daily Markdown files.
items.whyItMatters: Point Claude Code at the folder. It builds a work log for context, with no screenshots or OCR.
items.tryThis: Run the app, then ask Claude Code what you worked on Tuesday using its Markdown folder.

items.title: Pgbot: A 5.9 MB read-only Postgres tool for humans and agents
items.tldr: Pgbot is a 5.9 MB read-only command-line tool for querying Postgres, built for humans and agents.
items.whyItMatters: A tiny read-only binary gives an agent safe database access, with no write risk. It fits an unattended overnight run against production-like data.
items.tryThis: Download Pgbot and add it to your agent's toolset for safe Postgres queries.

items.title: v1.18.23
items.tldr: OpenCode 1.18.23 fixes Cloudflare AI Gateway routing, including Anthropic model ID conversion.
items.whyItMatters: This fix restores Anthropic and third-party model routing through Cloudflare AI Gateway. Update if you route calls there for cost control.
items.tryThis: Update OpenCode to 1.18.23 if you route model calls through Cloudflare AI Gateway.

items.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
items.tldr: Claude Desktop can now be configured to use Ollama as a third-party gateway, running open local models inside the Claude Desktop client.
items.whyItMatters: Lets you route cheap or sensitive subagent work to a free local model instead of paying for every call, without leaving the Claude Desktop UI.
items.tryThis: Add Ollama as a gateway provider in Claude Desktop settings and test a local model on a low-stakes subagent task.

items.title: LLMs could control their host machines by exploiting inference engines
items.tldr: Security researchers show LLMs can exploit inference-engine bugs to take control of the host machine running them.
items.whyItMatters: Unattended agents that call self-hosted inference engines inherit this attack surface. Treat the inference server as untrusted, not just the model output.
items.tryThis: Audit sandbox and network isolation on any self-hosted inference engine your agents can reach.

items.title: DietrichGebert/ponytail — Makes your AI agent think like the laziest senior dev in the room. The best code is the code you never wrote.
items.tldr: Ponytail is a new Claude Code skill that pushes agents to write less code.
items.whyItMatters: A drop-in behavior tweak could cut speculative code from agent PRs. Less code means a faster morning review.
items.tryThis: Clone DietrichGebert/ponytail and try it as a skill in Claude Code.

items.title: omnigent-ai/omnigent — Omnigent is an open-source AI agent framework and meta-harness: orchestrate Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Pi, and custom agents — swap harnesses without rewriting, enforce policies and sandboxing, and collaborate in rea
items.tldr: Omnigent is an open-source meta-harness that orchestrates Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and Pi from one policy layer, including from mobile.
items.whyItMatters: Adds sandboxing/policy enforcement across whatever agent CLI you already run and lets you check in from your phone.
items.tryThis: Try omnigent-ai/omnigent as a supervisor layer over your existing Claude Code worktree sessions to add policy checks and remote check-in.

items.title: trailhq/Graft — Turbocharge Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini & every coding agent: faster, cheaper, with contextual understanding specific to your codebase.
items.tldr: Graft adds a codebase-aware context layer to Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and Gemini that claims to cut cost and speed up runs.
items.whyItMatters: If the context layer works as advertised, it reduces token spend on every agent run without changing your existing tools.
items.tryThis: Install trailhq/Graft alongside Claude Code and compare token usage on a real task before and after.

items.title: Waishnav/devspace — Turn ChatGPT into Codex! OR Turn Claude Web into Claude Code!
items.tldr: devspace turns the ChatGPT or Claude web app into a Codex/Claude Code-style coding agent.
items.whyItMatters: Gives you a way to kick off or steer coding-agent runs from a phone browser without a CLI session.
items.tryThis: Try Waishnav/devspace from your phone browser to trigger an agent run when you're away from your terminal.

items.title: SaladDay/pi-from-scratch — 600 行 TypeScript 写成的超级迷你版 pi，让你轻松从 0 写出属于你的 pi-agent
items.tldr: SaladDay published pi-from-scratch, a 600-line TypeScript implementation that shows how to build a minimal coding agent.
items.whyItMatters: You can read the full agent loop in one sitting and reuse the parts you need for your own subagents or hooks.
items.tryThis: Clone SaladDay/pi-from-scratch and read the 600-line source to see the minimal agent loop.

items.title: Headlong: A microharness for persistent agents
items.tldr: Headlong is a new microharness built for running persistent, always-on agents.
items.whyItMatters: A small persistent-agent harness could replace your custom overnight loop code. Read it before you build your own.
items.tryThis: Check the Headlong repo and compare it to your current agent loop.

items.title: OpenAI restores 5-hour Codex and Work limits for ChatGPT Plus users
items.tldr: OpenAI reinstates a 5-hour usage cap on Codex and Work for ChatGPT Plus subscribers.
items.whyItMatters: If you lean on Codex through a Plus subscription for background coding runs, budget around the restored cap or move heavy work to the API.
items.tryThis: Check your Codex usage dashboard tonight and shift long unattended runs to API billing if you're near the 5-hour cap.

items.title: Mac Studio M5 Max Cost Analysis
items.tldr: A Reddit cost analysis shows a $10k Mac Studio M5 Max buys far fewer tokens than routing the same budget through cloud APIs like DeepSeek V4 Flash on OpenRouter.
items.whyItMatters: For a solo dev weighing local inference, cloud API credits still beat a high-end Mac Studio on pure token economics unless data sovereignty is the actual requirement.
items.tryThis: Skip the $10k Mac Studio; get a 24-32GB card for a mid-size local model and offload hard tasks to OpenRouter.

clusters.summary: Two separate projects add a completion-evidence-verification procedure on top of Opus and Claude Code, so an agent has to prove its work instead of just claiming it's done.

clusters.summary: opencodex proxies Codex/Claude Code calls to Ollama and other providers, and Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a gateway, letting you push cheap subagent work to a free local model.

clusters.summary: loop-engineering ships loop-audit and loop-cost to check an agent loop before an overnight run, and Headlong is a new microharness built specifically for persistent, always-on agents.

clusters.title: Steer agents from your phone
clusters.summary: devspace turns the ChatGPT or Claude web app into a coding-agent trigger from a browser, and omnigent adds a policy layer with mobile check-in over Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor sessions.
